annotate_invert — ANNOTATE overlay op

• Data kinds: image2d × mask → image2d

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.annotate_invert(img, mask, draw='fill', width=1.5, mode='complement', alpha=1.0, bits=128, min_contrast=1.5, on_invisible='warn') (to call the implementation directly, import annotate; annotate.annotate_invert(img, mask, draw='fill', width=1.5, mode='complement', alpha=1.0, bits=128, min_contrast=1.5, on_invisible='warn'); from the registry, opsannotate.get("annotate_invert"))

Usage

Fills / outlines a region in inverted color.

The classic trick for when "you do not know whether the ground is light or dark, so you want to draw in a colour visible on either". It spares you choosing a fill colour, but in exchange it vanishes in mid-tones, so the measurement of annotate_invert_visibility is always run internally.

★If the ground is monochrome (grey), first consider a saturated colour. Grey has no saturation, so a saturated colour is distinguishable from every level by hue -- more reliable than inverted colour, and moreover you can tell at a glance "this is an overlaid line" (pass a role colour to annotate_outline / overlay_mask). Inverted colour comes into its own when the ground is in colour and any colour you pick could clash. Note that what annotate_invert_visibility measures is the WCAG luminance ratio, so it cannot evaluate looks like "same luminance but different hue" -- if you draw with colour, do not rely on this op's numbers.

Parameters

mask : (H,W)

Region. Boolean or weights in [0,1]. A shape different from the image is an exception.

draw : {"fill", "margin"}

Same word as HALCON's set_draw. "fill" inverts including the interior, "margin"

inverts only the contour. The contour is a band width pixels thick (rounded to an integer)

that extends half inward and half outward from the region.

width : float

Band thickness (pixels) when draw="margin".

mode : str

INVERT_MODES. "complement" keeps the ground's pattern, "xor"

keeps the pattern while guaranteeing it does not vanish, and "contrast" falls back to black and white and

guarantees visibility.

bits : int

Bit mask for mode="xor" (1..255). The default 0x80 inverts only the most significant bit

-- it always jumps 128 levels, so it never vanishes. 0xFF is

the same as complement (cliff and all), and a mask of only low bits like 0x0F

is invisible at every level (measured: ratio below 1.5 at all 256 levels).

alpha : float

Strength of the inversion. 1.0 inverts fully, 0.5 is midway between ground and inverted colour

(mode="complement" at 0.5 always yields a mid-tone -- halving the inverted colour

naturally makes it vanish, and the warning catches that).

min_contrast, on_invisible :

What to do when it turns out invisible. "warn" (default) / "raise" (fail-closed)

/ "ignore".

Returns

(H,W[,C]) float64

A copy with the inversion applied. The input is not modified.

Raises

ValueError

shape mismatch / out of value range / unknown draw mode on_invisible /

invisible with on_invisible="raise".

Examples

>>> import numpy as np, annotate

>>> img = np.zeros((16, 16)); img[4:12, 4:12] = 1.0

>>> m = np.zeros((16, 16), bool); m[6:10, 6:10] = True

>>> out = annotate.annotate_invert(img, m)

>>> float(out[7, 7]), float(out[1, 1])

(0.0, 0.0)

>>> ring = annotate.annotate_invert(img, m, draw="margin", width=1)

>>> float(ring[7, 7]) # interior is untouched

1.0
